problem:
Calculate the value of 
$\,|\begin{aligned}1 & -6 & -2 & 4 \\ 2 & -3 & 7 & -5 \\ -2 & 3 & -1 & 2 \\ -2 & 3 & 1 & 7\end{aligned}|.$

*Hint: Use elementary row operations to make the entries above and below ${a}_{32}$ equal to zero. You should be able to reduce the given $4\times 4$ determinant to a $3\times 3$ determinant.*

activity_context.topic_title: Finding Determinants Using Row and Column Operations

feedback.problem:
Calculate the value of 
$\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 & -2 \\ 2 & 4 & 4 & -4 \\ -2 & 1 & -2 & -2\end{aligned}|.$

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the right of ${a}_{21}$ equal to zero. You should be able to reduce the given $4\times 4$ determinant to a $3\times 3$ determinant.*
feedback.worked_solution:
Using elementary column operations, let's make entries to the right of ${a}_{21}=1$ equal to zero.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 & -2 \\ 2 & 4 & 4 & -4 \\ -2 & 1 & -2 & -2\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+(-2){C}_{1} \\ {C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+(-3){C}_{1} \\ {C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+2{C}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & -2 & 0 \\ -2 & 5 & 4 & -6\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $2$nd row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & -2 & 0 \\ -2 & 5 & 4 & -6\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{2+1}|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 5 & 4 & -6\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 5 & 4 & -6\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-1)\cdot (-2)\cdot (-1)^{2+2}|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 5 & -6\end{aligned}| \\  & =2(-6-5) \\  & =-22.\end{aligned}
$$
